doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: Manuel Perez, Barbarin and George Lewis bands
summary: Russell and Laine discuss Manuel Perez's military band and Paul Barbarin and George Lewis bands playing music like Laine's.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: There was one man, the colored fellow had a band I heard of, Manuel Perez. Manuel Perez is a man. That's the man?
That's the man. Manuel Perez. That's the boy.
I mean Manuel had a good band.

He couldn't take it away from him. He was sort of a military band. He had a good band. Now there's only one band in this town that plays almost. Well, in fact, if you sit up, heard my band play and walk away and hear this colored band play, you'd hear my same stuff. What's his name? Paul Barbarian. Who? Barbarian. Barbarian. Barbarian. I guess that is. Barbarian. Barbarian. The same kind of stuff and almost the same temperature. They've got two, they've got two of those color bands as the same.
They both played for the Jazz at their auditorium one night. What's that other name of that other colored band?
I don't know, but that's when I discovered this Paul Barbario. I had his picture too.
I think you told me once before when we talked to you, it was George Lewis, I believe you said. Lewis, I believe Lewis, don't you know Lewis?
Lewis, the colored band, wasn't it Lewis?
The clarinet player, George Lewis, I think you told me before.
Oh, she's Barkay's brother, George Barkay.
Oh, I don't know about Barkay's brother. No, no. It was the two bands that played at the auditorium the night we were up there, the jazz club had
something. One of them sang that song.
Yeah, I believe that was Lewis, yes.
Yeah, I believe it was. I had his picture, but I don't know.
There was a couple of bands up there that night. There was a couple of bands up there.
That's the type of music that you played when you were up there.
